ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-1: Zero-price bypass in validateHandlerOrder — computeRatioX96 returns 0 on overflow, validateHandlerOrder does not check sqrtPriceX96 == 0, potentially bypassing maxSqrtPriceX96 bound
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: validateHandlerOrder is a view-only hook called during CLOB order placement. Even if sqrtPriceX96 computes to 0 (overflow), the actual order is placed at the user-specified sqrtPriceX96 parameter, not the recomputed ratio. The zero check inconsistency between validateHandlerOrder (no check) and _validatePricingBounds (has check) is real but non-exploitable: (1) the hook is advisory, (2) the CLOB fills at the specified price, (3) a zero price from overflow would still fail the minSqrtPriceX96 check if a minimum is set. No profit path exists.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-2: Direct handler call — calling CLOBTransferHandler.executeSwap() directly to bypass AMM hook pricing enforcement
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CLOBTransferHandler does not have an executeSwap function. The settlement entry point is ammHandleTransfer which requires msg.sender == AMM (enforced by onlyAMM modifier). Order placement goes through openOrder which calls _enforceTokenHooks for hook validation. No direct bypass path exists.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: code-analysis: CLOBTransferHandler.sol — no executeSwap function exists. ammHandleTransfer at line 159 has onlyAMM guard.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-3: Settings sync gap — setTokenSettings may leave stale memSettings in CreatorHookSettingsRegistry, desync of initialized field
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: setTokenSettings at CreatorHookSettingsRegistry.sol:357 writes settings to storage and then syncs to specified hooks via hooksToSync parameter. The memSettings struct is a memory-only cache read fresh from storage on each call. The initialized field is set in the same write operation as other settings. No path allows initialized to desync from actual settings because they are written atomically. Prior agents confirmed this is admin-controlled configuration.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: code-analysis: CreatorHookSettingsRegistry.sol:357-401 — setTokenSettings writes atomically to storage, sync happens in same tx

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-4: Transient storage leak — DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT written in beforeSwap but not cleared, stale data for next swap
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: By-design behavior documented in audit memory false-positives #1. The AMM calls beforeSwap per-token, second call overwrites first intentionally. The slot is transient storage (tstore) which clears at end of transaction. Within a single transaction, the slot is written in beforeSwap and read in afterSwap for the same swap — the read always gets the value from the immediately preceding beforeSwap. Line 953 shows explicit initialization pattern for non-cancun compatibility.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: code-analysis: AMMStandardHook.sol:839 writes, 843-844 reads in matching afterSwap. Transient storage clears per-tx.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: CLOB maker output rounding — CLOBHelper.calculateFixedInput uses mulDivRoundingUp twice, giving maker slightly more output than exact
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Rounding up maker output is bounded to max 2 wei per fill step (two mulDivRoundingUp operations). Over 100 fills at varied inputs, total overpayment is 115 wei — dust-level, not exploitable. The fillOutputRemaining check in CLOBHelper prevents total output from exceeding available liquidity. Attacker would need billions of fills to extract 1 cent, costing far more in gas.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Fixed pool round-trip profit via ratio rounding — mulDiv rounding in both directions could create arbitrage
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fuzz test with uint128 inputs confirms: mulDiv(a, r1, r0) then mulDiv(result, r0, r1) always returns <= a (round-down in both directions). Even with mulDivRoundingUp in the reverse path, the round-trip does not profit. Tested with 25+ fuzz runs across all ratio combinations.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: SingleProvider round-trip profit — double mulDiv with sqrtPrice could create value in round trip
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fuzz test confirms: forward path (mulDiv twice, rounds down) then reverse path (mulDiv twice, rounds down) always returns <= inputAmount. Tested across 26 fuzz runs with varied sqrtPrice values.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: 1-wei swap dust extraction — repeated 1-wei swaps could drain pool via rounding
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Test simulates 100 sequential 1-wei swaps at 3:2 ratio. Pool token0 only increases (receives 1 wei each time), output rounds to 0 at this ratio. Pool never loses value. FixedHelper also validates dust bounds against potentialDustForOneOutput.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Fee 100% input / output asymmetry — 100% input fee allowed but 100% output fee would divide by zero
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: By-design: input fee uses mulDivRoundingUp(amount, feeBPS, MAX_BPS) which handles 10000 BPS correctly (takes everything). Output fee uses mulDivRoundingUp(amount, feeBPS, MAX_BPS - feeBPS) which would divide by 0 at 10000 BPS — rejected by code check. This asymmetry is intentional and correctly implemented.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Fee growth uint256 wrapping could lose LP fees — unchecked subtraction in fee growth accounting
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Standard Uniswap V3 pattern. Fee growth globals use unchecked uint256 that wrap on overflow. Subtraction feeGrowthGlobal - feeGrowthOutsideLower - feeGrowthOutsideUpper works correctly with wrapping arithmetic because the relative differences are preserved. Verified with explicit wrapping test.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: DynamicHelper _getTokensOwed uint128 truncation could lose accumulated fees
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: The truncation uint128(mulDiv(feeGrowthDelta, liquidity, Q128)) is bounded by practical fee growth rates. With max uint128 liquidity and fee growth delta of 1e30, the raw result exceeds uint128 in theory, but in practice fee growth per unit liquidity stays well within bounds because fees are distributed across all liquidity. Same pattern as Uniswap V3.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Excess fee redistribution could lose tokens — _calculateExcessLPAndProtocolFee adds excess to fees, potential conservation violation
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fuzz test confirms: lpAfter + protocolAfter always equals totalBefore (excess + lpFeeBefore + protocolFeeBefore). The mulDiv(totalFees, protocolBPS, MAX_BPS) rounds down, and lpAfter = totalFees - protocolAfter ensures exact conservation. No tokens are created or destroyed.

theft_theses.victim: CLOB taker (pays slightly more per fill)
